new.analysis:
The signal from last week was clean, so a small step forward is appropriate. Pain stayed at 0/10 on Mon, Wed and Sat, your body check said the shin was quiet, and heart rate stayed in Z1 and Z2 the whole time. That is exactly the picture the physio's rule asks for before adding anything.

The change this week is to the length of each running interval, not the number of days. Last week your run segments were close to 1 minute; this week they move to 2 minutes, with a 1-minute walk between. That is a small, honest step and still well inside what you handled before the injury.

Three sessions, Mon, Wed and Sat, stays as the physio laid out. The 48 hours between runs is doing real work for the shin, so I am not tempted to add a fourth day yet. Total time on feet goes up only slightly, from about 45 to about 48 minutes across the week.

The rule for the week is simple: if the shin aches during a run, stop that session, and if it is sore the next morning, we repeat this week instead of adding next week. If it stays at 0/10 and quiet, we take the next small step together. Keep the physio's calf and hip routine on Tue and Thu.

settingsProposalBullets: Target of running 30 minutes continuously by mid-October — worth confirming so we can shape the next four weeks around it.

safetyCallouts.title: Stop any run if the shin aches.
safetyCallouts.body: Your physio set this rule, and it still applies. End the session, walk home, and let me know in your next check-in so we can repeat rather than progress. If the ache is sharp, lingers, or is worse the next morning, speak to your physio before the next run.
